Name of the insurance carrier or plan administrator providing this benefit (e.g., Aetna, BlueCross BlueShield, Fidelity, MetLife). Used for carrier invoicing reconciliation and employee ID card generation.
The insurance carrier's own plan identification number or group number assigned to this benefit plan. Required for claims processing, EOB reconciliation, and carrier EDI transactions.

Indicates whether this benefit plan is subject to COBRA continuation coverage requirements. Applies to employers with 20+ employees. Drives COBRA notice generation and premium calculation upon qualifying events.
Percentage of total premium charged to COBRA participants (typically 102% of total premium: 100% cost + 2% administrative fee). Used in COBRA billing calculations.
Percentage of covered medical expenses the employee pays after meeting the deductible (e.g., 20.00 means employee pays 20%, plan pays 80%). Used in employee benefits communications and cost modeling.
Fixed dollar copay amount an employee pays per primary care physician visit. Applicable to HMO and PPO medical plans.
Fixed dollar copay amount an employee pays per specialist physician visit.

Enrollment tier indicating who is covered under this benefit plan option. Determines premium amounts and dependent eligibility. Common tiers in restaurant industry: employee only, employee + spouse, employee + children, employee + family.
Annual out-of-pocket deductible amount for a family enrollment tier before the plan begins paying covered expenses.
Annual out-of-pocket deductible amount for an individual enrollee before the plan begins paying covered expenses. Applicable to medical and dental plans.
For short-term or long-term disability plans, the percentage of pre-disability base salary paid as a benefit (e.g., 60.00 = 60% of salary). Null for non-disability plan types.
Maximum weekly dollar benefit payable under a disability plan, regardless of the salary percentage calculation. Null for non-disability plan types.
Date on which this benefit plan becomes active and available for employee enrollment. Marks the start of the plan year or the date a new plan was introduced.

Employee classification tier that qualifies for this benefit plan. Restaurant operators commonly differentiate between full-time (30+ hrs/week), part-time, management, and executive tiers per ACA and ERISA nondiscrimination rules.

Per-pay-period dollar amount deducted from the employee's paycheck for this benefit plan (employee share of premium). Used in payroll integration with Workday HCM for pre-tax or post-tax deduction setup.
Annual dollar amount the employer seeds into the employee's Health Savings Account (HSA) for HDHP-enrolled employees. Used in total compensation reporting and payroll integration.
Per-pay-period dollar amount contributed by the employer toward this benefit plan. Used for labor cost modeling, benefits cost reporting, and ACA affordability calculations.
Three-digit plan number assigned by the employer for ERISA reporting purposes, used on DOL Form 5500 filings. Welfare benefit plans typically use numbers 501–999.
Date on which this benefit plan expires or is discontinued. Null for open-ended plans. Used to manage plan year transitions and open enrollment windows.
Indicates whether employees enrolled in this plan may also participate in a Flexible Spending Account (FSA) for healthcare or dependent care expenses.

Indicates how the benefit plan is financially structured. Fully insured plans transfer risk to the carrier; self-funded plans retain risk with the employer. Impacts stop-loss insurance requirements and DOL Form 5500 reporting.
Employer group number assigned by the insurance carrier, printed on employee insurance cards and used for claims submission and provider verification.

Indicates whether this plan qualifies as a High-Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) making enrollees eligible to open and contribute to a Health Savings Account (HSA). Drives IRS contribution limit enforcement.

Indicates whether this plan meets the ACA affordability threshold (employee premium does not exceed the IRS-published percentage of household income). Critical for avoiding ACA employer shared responsibility penalties.
Indicates whether this plan qualifies as Minimum Essential Coverage (MEC) under the Affordable Care Act. Required for ACA employer mandate compliance reporting on IRS Forms 1094-C and 1095-C.
Indicates whether this plan meets the ACA Minimum Value standard (covers at least 60% of total allowed costs). Required for ACA affordability and employer shared responsibility compliance.
For life insurance plans, the multiple of annual salary used to calculate the death benefit (e.g., 1.0 = 1x salary, 2.0 = 2x salary). Null for non-life-insurance plan types.
Maximum dollar cap on the life insurance death benefit regardless of salary multiple. Amounts above IRS Section 79 threshold ($50,000) trigger imputed income calculations.
Indicates the provider network scope for this plan. Relevant for restaurant employees who may work across multiple geographic locations and need portable coverage.
Free-text field for HR administrators to capture plan-specific notes, special eligibility conditions, carrier contact information, or renewal negotiation details not captured in structured fields.
Date on which the annual open enrollment window closes. Elections made after this date require a qualifying life event (QLE) to be processed.
Date on which the annual open enrollment window opens for this benefit plan, allowing employees to elect, change, or waive coverage for the upcoming plan year.
Maximum annual out-of-pocket cost for a family enrollment tier, after which the plan covers 100% of covered expenses.
Maximum annual out-of-pocket cost for an individual enrollee, after which the plan covers 100% of covered expenses. ACA mandates annual limits for essential health benefits.
Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the benefit plan, used in HR systems, payroll integration, and employee communications (e.g., MED-PPO-FULL, DEN-BASIC-PT).
Human-readable name of the benefit plan as displayed to employees during open enrollment and in HR portals (e.g., 'Full-Time Medical PPO Gold', 'Part-Time Dental Basic').

Current lifecycle state of the benefit plan. Active plans are available for enrollment; discontinued plans retain historical enrollments but accept no new members; grandfathered plans are ACA-exempt legacy offerings.
Further classification within the plan type, such as PPO vs HMO for medical, or term vs whole for life insurance. Determines network access, cost-sharing structure, and IRS contribution limits.

Category of benefit covered by this plan. Drives eligibility rules, tax treatment, and payroll deduction logic. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: medical|dental|vision|life_insurance|disability|401k|fsa|hsa|commuter|supplemental|eap|pet|legal — promote to reference product]
Calendar month (1–12) in which the plan year begins. Determines open enrollment timing, FSA/HSA contribution reset dates, and deductible accumulation periods.
Frequency at which premium deductions are taken from employee paychecks. Must align with the restaurant's payroll cycle configured in Workday HCM.
Indicates whether mid-year enrollment changes are permitted upon a qualifying life event (e.g., marriage, birth, loss of other coverage). Required for HIPAA special enrollment compliance.
Self-referencing FK on benefit_plan (replaces_benefit_plan_id)

Name of the insurance carrier or plan administrator providing this benefit (e.g., Aetna, BlueCross BlueShield, Fidelity, MetLife). Used for carrier invoicing reconciliation and employee ID card generation.
The insurance carrier's own plan identification number or group number assigned to this benefit plan. Required for claims processing, EOB reconciliation, and carrier EDI transactions.

Indicates whether this benefit plan is subject to COBRA continuation coverage requirements. Applies to employers with 20+ employees. Drives COBRA notice generation and premium calculation upon qualifying events.
Percentage of total premium charged to COBRA participants (typically 102% of total premium: 100% cost + 2% administrative fee). Used in COBRA billing calculations.
Percentage of covered medical expenses the employee pays after meeting the deductible (e.g., 20.00 means employee pays 20%, plan pays 80%). Used in employee benefits communications and cost modeling.
Fixed dollar copay amount an employee pays per primary care physician visit. Applicable to HMO and PPO medical plans.
Fixed dollar copay amount an employee pays per specialist physician visit.

Enrollment tier indicating who is covered under this benefit plan option. Determines premium amounts and dependent eligibility. Common tiers in restaurant industry: employee only, employee + spouse, employee + children, employee + family.
Annual out-of-pocket deductible amount for a family enrollment tier before the plan begins paying covered expenses.
Annual out-of-pocket deductible amount for an individual enrollee before the plan begins paying covered expenses. Applicable to medical and dental plans.
For short-term or long-term disability plans, the percentage of pre-disability base salary paid as a benefit (e.g., 60.00 = 60% of salary). Null for non-disability plan types.
Maximum weekly dollar benefit payable under a disability plan, regardless of the salary percentage calculation. Null for non-disability plan types.
Date on which this benefit plan becomes active and available for employee enrollment. Marks the start of the plan year or the date a new plan was introduced.

Employee classification tier that qualifies for this benefit plan. Restaurant operators commonly differentiate between full-time (30+ hrs/week), part-time, management, and executive tiers per ACA and ERISA nondiscrimination rules.

Per-pay-period dollar amount deducted from the employee's paycheck for this benefit plan (employee share of premium). Used in payroll integration with Workday HCM for pre-tax or post-tax deduction setup.
Annual dollar amount the employer seeds into the employee's Health Savings Account (HSA) for HDHP-enrolled employees. Used in total compensation reporting and payroll integration.
Per-pay-period dollar amount contributed by the employer toward this benefit plan. Used for labor cost modeling, benefits cost reporting, and ACA affordability calculations.
Three-digit plan number assigned by the employer for ERISA reporting purposes, used on DOL Form 5500 filings. Welfare benefit plans typically use numbers 501–999.
Date on which this benefit plan expires or is discontinued. Null for open-ended plans. Used to manage plan year transitions and open enrollment windows.
Indicates whether employees enrolled in this plan may also participate in a Flexible Spending Account (FSA) for healthcare or dependent care expenses.

Indicates how the benefit plan is financially structured. Fully insured plans transfer risk to the carrier; self-funded plans retain risk with the employer. Impacts stop-loss insurance requirements and DOL Form 5500 reporting.
Employer group number assigned by the insurance carrier, printed on employee insurance cards and used for claims submission and provider verification.

Indicates whether this plan qualifies as a High-Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) making enrollees eligible to open and contribute to a Health Savings Account (HSA). Drives IRS contribution limit enforcement.

Indicates whether this plan meets the ACA affordability threshold (employee premium does not exceed the IRS-published percentage of household income). Critical for avoiding ACA employer shared responsibility penalties.
Indicates whether this plan qualifies as Minimum Essential Coverage (MEC) under the Affordable Care Act. Required for ACA employer mandate compliance reporting on IRS Forms 1094-C and 1095-C.
Indicates whether this plan meets the ACA Minimum Value standard (covers at least 60% of total allowed costs). Required for ACA affordability and employer shared responsibility compliance.
For life insurance plans, the multiple of annual salary used to calculate the death benefit (e.g., 1.0 = 1x salary, 2.0 = 2x salary). Null for non-life-insurance plan types.
Maximum dollar cap on the life insurance death benefit regardless of salary multiple. Amounts above IRS Section 79 threshold ($50,000) trigger imputed income calculations.
Indicates the provider network scope for this plan. Relevant for restaurant employees who may work across multiple geographic locations and need portable coverage.
Free-text field for HR administrators to capture plan-specific notes, special eligibility conditions, carrier contact information, or renewal negotiation details not captured in structured fields.
Date on which the annual open enrollment window closes. Elections made after this date require a qualifying life event (QLE) to be processed.
Date on which the annual open enrollment window opens for this benefit plan, allowing employees to elect, change, or waive coverage for the upcoming plan year.
Maximum annual out-of-pocket cost for a family enrollment tier, after which the plan covers 100% of covered expenses.
Maximum annual out-of-pocket cost for an individual enrollee, after which the plan covers 100% of covered expenses. ACA mandates annual limits for essential health benefits.
Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the benefit plan, used in HR systems, payroll integration, and employee communications (e.g., MED-PPO-FULL, DEN-BASIC-PT).
Human-readable name of the benefit plan as displayed to employees during open enrollment and in HR portals (e.g., 'Full-Time Medical PPO Gold', 'Part-Time Dental Basic').

Current lifecycle state of the benefit plan. Active plans are available for enrollment; discontinued plans retain historical enrollments but accept no new members; grandfathered plans are ACA-exempt legacy offerings.
Further classification within the plan type, such as PPO vs HMO for medical, or term vs whole for life insurance. Determines network access, cost-sharing structure, and IRS contribution limits.

Category of benefit covered by this plan. Drives eligibility rules, tax treatment, and payroll deduction logic. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: medical|dental|vision|life_insurance|disability|401k|fsa|hsa|commuter|supplemental|eap|pet|legal — promote to reference product]
Calendar month (1–12) in which the plan year begins. Determines open enrollment timing, FSA/HSA contribution reset dates, and deductible accumulation periods.
Frequency at which premium deductions are taken from employee paychecks. Must align with the restaurant's payroll cycle configured in Workday HCM.
Indicates whether mid-year enrollment changes are permitted upon a qualifying life event (e.g., marriage, birth, loss of other coverage). Required for HIPAA special enrollment compliance.
